_note: Faith workbook research, 7 October 2026. Companion to docs/research/faith-workbooks.md. Verified means the author, translator and editor death years and the first publication year were found in at least one source listed. Every title still needs the house public-domain record (docs/public-domain/) and a signed review before use.

rules.GB: life plus 70 years from the end of the year of death of the last author, translator or editor
rules.IE: life plus 70 years from the end of the year of death of the last author, translator or editor (EU rule)
rules.tier_A: published before 1931 and every author, translator and editor died before 1946 (Research 4)
rules.CA_AU_NZ: not recorded in the repo; to confirm by the Legal Lead

field_values.subcategory: slugs from the Faith and Spirituality category in docs/research/taxonomy.json (draft)

titles.author: Brother Lawrence (Nicolas Herman)
titles.title: The Practice of the Presence of God
titles.first_published: 1692 (French, as Maximes spirituelles, compiled by Joseph de Beaufort)
titles.pd_edition: 'The Practice of the Presence of God the Best Rule of a Holy Life', Fleming H. Revell, New York, anonymous translation, Project Gutenberg eBook #13871. Do NOT use eBook #5657: it is the 2002 Lightheart edition and is marked copyrighted.
titles.uk_status: clear: author died 1691; the Revell translation is anonymous, so the UK term runs 70 years from publication, long expired [confirm the Revell printing year]
titles.us_status: clear: Gutenberg #13871 is marked public domain in the USA; printed by Revell well before 1931 [confirm year]
titles.angle: 6 weeks. Weeks 1 to 2 the four conversations; weeks 3 to 6 the letters. Each week one practice of turning to God in ordinary work, with a short daily noticing log.

titles.author: Thomas a Kempis
titles.title: The Imitation of Christ
titles.pd_edition: Translation by William Benham (1831 to 1910), Project Gutenberg eBook #1653 (also #26222)
titles.uk_status: clear: author died 1471; translator Benham died 1910, so the translation term ended at the end of 1980
titles.us_status: clear: Gutenberg marks it public domain in the USA; Benham died 1910, so a translation he made appeared before 1931 unless issued long after his death [confirm the translation year]
titles.angle: 12 weeks. Books 1 and 2 over weeks 1 to 5, Book 3 over weeks 6 to 10, Book 4 (the Eucharist) over weeks 11 to 12 or offered as optional for non-Catholic groups. One short chapter a day with a reflection line.

titles.author: John Bunyan
titles.title: The Pilgrim's Progress
titles.pd_edition: Project Gutenberg eBook #131 (17th-century text, no modern editor credited)
titles.us_status: clear: first published 1678; Gutenberg marks it public domain in the USA
titles.angle: 12 weeks on Part I, one stage of the journey a week (Wicket Gate, Interpreter's House, Vanity Fair, Doubting Castle and so on), with a map of the reader's own journey. Part II could be a later 8-week sequel.

titles.author: Andrew Murray
titles.title: Abide in Christ
titles.first_published: 1880 (J. Nisbet, per the Online Books Page listing); Wikipedia gives 1882 [confirm]
titles.pd_edition: 1880 Nisbet or 1895 Revell edition, page images at HathiTrust via the Online Books Page
titles.us_status: clear: published 1880 or 1882, before 1931
titles.angle: 6 weeks over the 31 short chapters, about five a week, each with one verse to carry through the day and a short abiding prayer.

titles.author: Andrew Murray
titles.title: With Christ in the School of Prayer
titles.pd_edition: 1885 Revell or 1887 Nisbet edition (HathiTrust); HTML at CCEL [check CCEL terms of use]
titles.us_status: clear: published 1885
titles.angle: 6 weeks over the 31 lessons, about five a week, each ending with Murray's own prayer and a reader's prayer journal entry.

titles.author: Andrew Murray
titles.title: Humility: The Beauty of Holiness
titles.pd_edition: Project Gutenberg eBook #57121
titles.us_status: clear: published 1895; Gutenberg marks it public domain in the USA
titles.angle: 6 weeks, two of the twelve chapters a week, with a weekly practice of noticing pride and serving someone unseen.

titles.author: Andrew Murray
titles.title: Absolute Surrender and Other Addresses
titles.pd_edition: Project Gutenberg eBook #19572
titles.us_status: clear: published 1895; Gutenberg marks it public domain in the USA
titles.angle: 4 weeks, two or three addresses a week, each with one honest question and one small act of trust.

titles.author: C. H. Spurgeon
titles.title: Morning and Evening
titles.first_published: Morning by Morning 1865; Evening by Evening 1868
titles.pd_edition: 19th-century text as hosted at CCEL [confirm CCEL source edition and terms]. Avoid modern revised editions with updated Bible text.
titles.us_status: clear: published 1865 and 1868
titles.angle: 12 weeks (one season), using the daily readings as the daily check and a weekly review. The schema allows up to 52 units, so a full-year edition of 52 weeks is possible later.

titles.author: C. H. Spurgeon
titles.title: All of Grace
titles.pd_edition: 1886 London or R. Carter (New York) edition; text at spurgeon.org and CCEL [confirm source edition]
titles.us_status: clear: published 1886
titles.angle: 6 weeks for enquirers and new Christians: grace, faith, repentance and assurance, about three short chapters a week.

titles.author: E. M. Bounds
titles.title: Power Through Prayer
titles.first_published: 1907, as Preacher and Prayer; later republished as Power Through Prayer
titles.pd_edition: Marshall Brothers, London, twelfth edition, Project Gutenberg eBook #65115 [confirm printing year]
titles.uk_status: clear: author died 1913; this title was published in his lifetime, so no later editor applies
titles.us_status: clear: first published 1907; Gutenberg marks it public domain in the USA
titles.angle: 4 weeks for preachers, small group leaders and church teams: five short chapters a week, with a leader's prayer plan.

titles.author: Augustine of Hippo
titles.title: Confessions
titles.pd_edition: Translation by E. B. Pusey (1800 to 1882), first published 1838, Project Gutenberg eBook #3296. Do not use Outler (1955), Pine-Coffin (1961) or Chadwick (2008), which are later and in copyright in the UK.
titles.uk_status: clear: Pusey died 1882, so the translation term ended at the end of 1952
titles.us_status: clear: Pusey translation published 1838; Gutenberg marks it public domain in the USA
titles.angle: 12 weeks. Books 1 to 9 (the life) over weeks 1 to 9; Books 10 to 13 (memory, time, creation) over weeks 10 to 12 as a guided study.

titles.author: Hannah Whitall Smith
titles.title: The Christian's Secret of a Happy Life
titles.pd_edition: 1875 Willard or 1883 Revell edition (HathiTrust); HTML at CCEL [confirm source]. Avoid modern abridged or 'unabridged' reissues with new apparatus.
titles.us_status: clear: published 1875
titles.angle: 8 weeks on trust, surrender, doubts, temptation and failure, about three chapters a week, framed as a devotional, never as a route to happiness.

titles.author: Charles M. Sheldon
titles.title: In His Steps
titles.pd_edition: Project Gutenberg eBook #4540
titles.uk_status: clear: author died 1946, so the UK term ended at the end of 2016. Research 4 Tier B, not Tier A, because the death year is not before 1946.
titles.us_status: clear: published 1896; Gutenberg marks it public domain in the USA
titles.angle: 6 weeks as a book group: about five chapters a week, each week asking 'What would Jesus do?' about one real decision at work, at home or with money.

titles.author: Francis de Sales
titles.title: Introduction to the Devout Life
titles.pd_edition: An Introduction to the Devout Life, M. H. Gill and Son, Dublin, 1885, anonymous translation 'carefully revised and compared with the latest French edition' (scan at wesleyscholar.com; HathiTrust holds 1873 to 1906 editions). Avoid Ryan (1950s onward) and Ross (1924) unless cleared.
titles.uk_status: clear: author died 1622; the 1885 translation is anonymous, so the term ran 70 years from publication and has expired [confirm no named translator]
titles.us_status: clear: 1885 edition, before 1931
titles.angle: 8 weeks following the five parts: the call to devotion, prayer, virtues in daily life, temptations, and renewal. Written for lay people with ordinary jobs and families.

titles.author: William Law
titles.title: A Serious Call to a Devout and Holy Life
titles.pd_edition: 1729 Innys or a 19th-century reprint (HathiTrust); CCEL text [confirm source]. Do not reproduce the Charles Bigg introductions (1899 onward) without checking Bigg's dates.
titles.us_status: clear: published 1729
titles.angle: 8 weeks, three chapters a week, using Law's character sketches (Calidus, Flavia, Miranda) as prompts to audit how the reader spends time and money.

titles.author: Jonathan Edwards
titles.title: A Treatise Concerning Religious Affections
titles.pd_edition: 1746 Boston text (Evans TCP) or 1821 Philadelphia edition (HathiTrust)
titles.us_status: clear: published 1746
titles.angle: 12 weeks as a study group: weeks 1 to 2 Parts I and II, then one of Edwards' twelve signs of genuine faith each week in Part III, read in short selections.

titles.author: J. C. Ryle
titles.title: Holiness: Its Nature, Hindrances, Difficulties and Roots
titles.pd_edition: 1879 enlarged edition (page images via HathiTrust or archive.org); HTML at anglicanlibrary.org [confirm source]. Avoid modern editions with forewords.
titles.us_status: clear: published 1877 and 1879
titles.angle: 8 weeks, two or three papers a week, on sin, sanctification, the fight, cost and growth.

titles.author: J. C. Ryle
titles.title: Practical Religion
titles.pd_edition: Project Gutenberg eBook #38162
titles.us_status: clear: published 1878; Gutenberg marks it public domain in the USA
titles.angle: 8 weeks on the daily duties of the Christian life (self-inquiry, prayer, Bible reading, charity, family, money), about three papers a week. The paper on sickness needs Help now.

titles.author: George Müller
titles.title: A Narrative of Some of the Lord's Dealings with George Müller
titles.first_published: In parts during Müller's lifetime [confirm year of Part 1]
titles.pd_edition: Project Gutenberg eBooks #20379 (Part 1), #22034 (Part 2), #22148 (Part 3), #20245 (Part 4)
titles.us_status: clear: Gutenberg marks it public domain in the USA; the parts were issued during his lifetime [confirm each part's year]
titles.angle: 6 weeks of selected passages on prayer, trust and the Bristol orphan houses, with a weekly prayer record. Not a money workbook.

titles.author: Julian of Norwich
titles.title: Revelations of Divine Love
titles.first_published: Late 14th to early 15th century manuscript; Warrack edition 1901
titles.pd_edition: Edited by Grace Warrack (1855 to 1932), Methuen, London, 1901, Project Gutenberg eBook #52958
titles.uk_status: clear: Warrack died 1932, so her editorial term ended at the end of 2002
titles.us_status: clear: published 1901; Gutenberg marks it public domain in the USA
titles.angle: 8 weeks, two of the sixteen showings a week, with slow reading and a short contemplative exercise.

titles.author: Henry Drummond
titles.title: The Greatest Thing in the World
titles.pd_edition: Project Gutenberg eBook #16739 (with other addresses)
titles.us_status: clear: published 1890; Gutenberg marks it public domain in the USA
titles.angle: 4 weeks on 1 Corinthians 13: Drummond's nine 'ingredients' of love (patience, kindness, generosity and so on), one practised each few days.

titles.author: G. K. Chesterton
titles.title: Orthodoxy
titles.pd_edition: Project Gutenberg eBook #130
titles.uk_status: clear: author died 1936, so the UK term ended at the end of 2006
titles.us_status: clear: published 1908; Gutenberg marks it public domain in the USA
titles.angle: 8 weeks as a discussion group on reasons for faith, roughly one chapter a week.

titles.author: R. A. Torrey
titles.title: How to Pray
titles.pd_edition: 1900 Revell edition (HathiTrust); CCEL text [confirm source]
titles.us_status: clear: published 1900
titles.angle: 4 weeks, two chapters a week, building a simple daily prayer pattern.

titles.author: Evelyn Underhill
titles.title: Practical Mysticism: A Little Book for Normal People
titles.pd_edition: Project Gutenberg eBook #21774
titles.uk_status: clear: author died 1941, so the UK term ended at the end of 2011
titles.us_status: clear: published 1914; Gutenberg marks it public domain in the USA
titles.angle: 6 weeks on attention, recollection and contemplation, with short guided practices. Framed as prayer, not as a wellbeing technique.

titles.author: George MacDonald
titles.title: Unspoken Sermons (Series I, II and III)
titles.first_published: Series I 1867 (A. Strahan, as Epea aptera: unspoken sermons); later series [confirm years]
titles.pd_edition: Project Gutenberg eBook #9057
titles.us_status: clear: Series I 1867; Gutenberg marks the three series public domain in the USA [confirm Series II and III years]
titles.angle: 12 weeks of selected sermons, one a week, with a close-reading guide and discussion questions.

titles.author: Ignatius of Loyola, adapted by Charles Coppens
titles.title: The Spiritual Exercises of St. Ignatius, adapted to an eight days retreat
titles.first_published: Exercises composed about 1522 to 1524; Coppens adaptation B. Herder, 1916
titles.pd_edition: Coppens adaptation, B. Herder, 1916, Project Gutenberg eBook #70790
titles.uk_status: clear: Coppens died 1920, so his term ended at the end of 1990
titles.us_status: clear: published 1916; Gutenberg marks it public domain in the USA
titles.angle: 8 days (unit: day) as a retreat at home, one day of meditations each, with a companion or group leader guide. Coppens wrote for Jesuits, so the lay framing is new Akana material.

titles.author: Matthew Henry
titles.title: A Method for Prayer
titles.pd_edition: 1710 edition (HathiTrust, Google Books) or 1834 Glasgow edition (archive.org). Do not use the 2013 modernised edition at mrmatthewhenry.com, which has new editorial work.
titles.us_status: clear: published 1710
titles.angle: 6 weeks following Henry's parts: adoration, confession, petition, thanksgiving, intercession and a week on putting it together, praying Scripture's own words.

excluded.author: Oswald Chambers (compiled by Gertrude 'Biddy' Chambers)
excluded.title: My Utmost for His Highest
excluded.first_published: Self-published about 1924; Simpkin and Marshall 1927; US (Dodd, Mead) 1935
excluded.uk_status: not clear: the text was compiled by his widow from her own shorthand notes of his talks. Under Walter v Lane (1900) a verbatim reporter can hold copyright in the report, so her term may run to the end of 2036. Treat as in copyright [Legal Lead to rule].
excluded.us_status: not clear: US edition 1935, copyright renewed in 1963, so protected until the end of 2030
excluded.angle: Excluded. Approach the rights holder if wanted.

excluded.author: A. W. Tozer
excluded.title: The Pursuit of God
excluded.uk_status: not clear: author died 1963, so in copyright in the UK and EU until the end of 2033
excluded.us_status: Gutenberg marks it public domain in the USA
excluded.angle: Excluded. US-only title; Akana sells in the UK first. Revisit in 2034.

excluded.author: Dietrich Bonhoeffer
excluded.title: The Cost of Discipleship (Nachfolge) and Life Together (Gemeinsames Leben)
excluded.first_published: Nachfolge 1937; Gemeinsames Leben 1939; English translations 1948 (R. H. Fuller) and 1954
excluded.pd_edition: German originals only, in the UK and EU
excluded.uk_status: German text clear: author died 1945, so the term ended at the end of 2015. The English translations are later and in copyright. A new Akana translation would be possible.
excluded.us_status: not clear: German texts first published 1937 and 1939, after 1930, so not public domain in the US yet [confirm the US term for foreign works]
excluded.angle: Excluded for now. Possible UK-only new translation later.

excluded.author: Amy Carmichael
excluded.title: If (and later devotional books)
excluded.first_published: If 1938; Gold by Moonlight 1935; Edges of His Ways 1955
excluded.pd_edition: none for the devotional books in the US
excluded.uk_status: clear: author died 1951, so the UK term ended at the end of 2021
excluded.us_status: not clear: these were published after 1930; renewal not checked. Her pre-1931 books (Things as They Are 1903, Lotus Buds 1909, Made in the Pans 1918) are clear in the US but are mission narratives and verse, not devotional workbooks.
